headline: High risk: Roo Code’s default filesystem/network/tool access can amplify Caveman outputs into prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can use MCP and writes/reads project notes and CLAUDE.md, while Roo Code uses MCP, reads/writes workspace files, and runs browsers. That creates a default shared-content pathway where Caveman output can be consumed by Roo Code as instructions. No direct provenance controls are shown, so injection risk is plausible but not proven high.
conditions: IF Caveman writes attacker-controlled text into shared workspace files or MCP messages
IF Roo Code ingests those files or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Disable MCP on one side for shared tasks
Add a manual review step before Roo Code follows Caveman-authored text
Use allowlisted file paths only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; Roo Code has broad network egress, reads/writes workspace files, and handles model-provider API keys. If they share a workspace, sensitive content from Caveman can flow into Roo Code and then out to third-party APIs. The shared-workspace path is explicit in Roo Code, while Caveman’s local-only egress is not enough to block leakage.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or project notes
IF Roo Code sends shared file contents to its configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Separate sensitive notes from the shared workspace
Turn off network access for Roo Code on sensitive tasks
Rotate any exposed API keys
Limit Caveman output to non-sensitive summaries
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and uses files, while Roo Code supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem, plus write_filesystem and modify_git_state. In a shared repo, both can mutate the same files and git state without any locking mechanism shown. That is a direct conflict pathway in default usage and can corrupt work or overwrite changes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF either agent edits files or git state concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Review diffs before any commit
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces content-writing outputs and can use MCP, while Roo Code can act on workspace files, browsers, shell, and git. If Roo Code treats Caveman’s output as authoritative, it can turn a writing error into code changes, browser actions, or commits. The pair lacks any documented verification gate, so the cascade risk is substantial.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Caveman output as a source of truth
IF Roo Code executes shell, browser, or git actions based on that output without verification
mitigations: Require human approval before actions
Cross-check Caveman outputs against source material
Limit Roo Code to read-only review mode
Use a second independent verifier
requires-engineering: add structured citations and validation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys with broad network egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through logs and external API calls. No single cited control shows harmonized compliance handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Caveman-managed notes or logs
IF Roo Code forwards that data to external model APIs or retains screenshots
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Disable screenshot capture for sensitive sessions
Use a compliant model endpoint only
Set short retention on logs and notes
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy
